newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russian, Bulgarian firms cooperate on electricity.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Bulgarian firms cooperate on electricity.

text.p: Russian gas giant RAO Gazprom, RAO United Energy Systems (UES) and Bulgarian conglomerate Multigroup have agreed to operate a Balkan centre for electricity supplies, Multigroup's president said.
"The new agreement marks the establishment of an informal Balkan energy centre," Multigroup president Ilia Pavlov told Kontinent daily in an interview published on Monday.

Gazprom's president Rem Vyakhirev, UES president Anatolii Dyakov and Pavlov signed a memorandum for joint activities such as production, sale and transiting of electricity to the Balkans on October 5 in Moscow.
The new project, named Topenergy-2, is also aimed at uniting the three companies' investment in the energy field, Pavlov said.
Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov was informed about the project during a meeting with Pavlov last week in Skopje.
"We do not expect to face the problems we had with Topenergy," Pavlov said.

Gazprom, which holds 50 percent in the Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy, is still awaiting Bulgaria's delayed decision on granting a concession for selling and delivering Russian gas to the Balkans via Bulgaria.
Multigroup and its gas arm Overgas Inc, which is half-owned by Gazprom, have 8.25 percent each.
The remaining half is distributed among Bulgarian participants, including Bulgargas which holds 25.1 percent.
Topenergy was at odds with Bulgaria's socialist government earlier this year when the cabinet insisted on stronger state participation and control of the venture.
